description: Everything that defines a run, fixed before its first event

driver.description: The id of the driver that answers for the actor, for example `fake/sample` or `scripted`

grant.description: The name of the grant the actor's tools come from

kind.description: The kind of the actor, the part of its id before the colon

model.description: The model behind the actor; absent for a fake or scripted driver

params.description: The sampling parameters; every field is a value or `provider-default`, never absent

anyOf.description: The value that was sent to the provider

maxOutputTokens.description: The limit of output tokens of one request

anyOf.description: The value that was sent to the provider

thinking.description: The thinking setting of the model, as the driver names it

anyOf.description: The value that was sent to the provider

pricing.description: The price table the cost of the run is computed with, as `<library>@<version>`

provider.description: The provider the requests go to

requestedId.description: The model id as the command gave it, an alias included

resolvedId.description: The model id after the alias was resolved

textHashes.description: The hashes of the texts the actor is shown, by part: `briefing`, `tools` (the tool list as shown) and, for a model actor, `system` (the whole system prompt as sent) and `toolSpecs` (name, description and parameter schema of every granted tool, in grant order)

experiment.description: Set when the run is part of an experiment

arm.description: The arm of the experiment the run belongs to

specHash.description: The sha256 of the experiment's specification

format.description: The name of the manifest format

hash.description: The sha256 of the canonical JSON of the resolved game definition (`game.json`)

params.description: The parameters the game was started with, by name

^.*$.description: The value of one parameter; it must be a JSON value, which the manifest builder guarantees

title.description: The title of the game, for a reader

human.description: Set when the game has the actor `human`: a person may intervene in the run. Absent otherwise, never `false`

kernel.description: The kernel that ran the game

commit.description: The commit of the platform's source tree

dirty.description: Whether the source tree had changes that are not committed

node.description: The version of Node.js that ran the kernel

revision.description: The runtime revision of the kernel; it rises when the way a run plays changes

version.description: The package version of the kernel

limits.description: The limits the run stops at

budgetUsd.description: The money the run may spend, in US dollars

maxCallsPerTick.description: The most tool calls one actor may make in one tick

maxTicks.description: The tick after which the run ends at the latest

log.description: The format of the event log the run writes

format.description: The name of the log format

version.description: The version of the log format

naming.description: The version of the naming rules for ids and event types

plugins.description: The plugins of the run, in load order

id.description: The id of the plugin inside the game

optionsHash.description: The sha256 of the canonical JSON of the plugin's options

package.description: The name of the package the plugin comes from

replicate.description: The index of the repetition: same seed, other sampling

resumedFrom.description: Set when the run resumes from a snapshot

snapshotHash.description: The sha256 of the snapshot the run started from

id.description: The id of the run, also the name of its folder

purpose.description: What the run is for; it decides how strict the runner is and whether results may be pooled

startedAt.description: The wall-clock time the run started at, as an ISO 8601 string

scheduler.description: The scheduler that decided who acts when

determinism.description: What the scheduler promises about repeating a run with the same seed

id.description: The id of the scheduler; an open id, not a closed list

options.description: The options the scheduler was given; they must be a JSON value, which the manifest builder guarantees, so that `optionsHash` is defined

optionsHash.description: The sha256 of the canonical JSON of the scheduler's options

revision.description: The revision of the scheduler; it rises when its order of activations changes

seed.description: The seed of the world, a 32-bit number: deals, order and lots follow from it

texts.description: The hash of every plugin text and kernel reply, by key

version.description: The version of the manifest format
